title: 1920s The Observer Office, Fred Stevens, the Editor was on right
description: Fred Stevens (1873–1924) received his first printing press at age 13. In 1897, he began publishing “The Advertiser” as Hartland’s first weekly newspaper; previously, it had been a monthly. Ill health forced Stevens to stop in 1904, and George MacLauchlan of Woodstock temporarily filled the gap with his paper, “The Chat,” until his building was lost in the 1907 fire. MacLauchlan gave up publishing the Chat in 1909. On June 4, 1909, Stevens launched “The Observer” from a cement block building on Orser Street, just past the railroad tracks. In 1920, he moved the operation to a Main Street building across from the bridge ramp. That building was demolished in 2001.
